source.title: Extraction and Analysis of Multimodal Concepts in Vision Language Models through Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Sergio Lanza; Jae Hee Lee; Stefan Wermter

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some table layout is flattened; Appendix Table 7 does not clearly associate its displayed numbers with the stated similarity measure or dataset columns.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE-based concept extraction and evaluation to a vision-language model and reports results bearing on whether SAE features can be identified and interpreted in that new setting. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates concept extraction and alignment for SAE neurons, including comparison with a baseline. It does not measure feature overlap, direction geometry, or capacity competition. The choice of the 24th layer and fixed intervention strength are methodological choices, not results. The qualitative activation intervention is recorded as a finding about induced output changes, not as evidence that features arise naturally.
record.test_reason: The study takes a pretrained SAE on LLaVA-NeXT-8B as a tool. It reports how well its own concept-labelling pipeline (explainer prompts plus CLIP/ALIGN scoring) performs against the Zhang et al. baseline. Nearly every number compares one explanation method with another or counts hypotheses the pipeline produced. None measures whether the model's features are superposed or distributed across neurons, whether a dictionary recovers sparse features (reconstruction or sparsity are not evaluated), or whether SAE features are stable or canonical. The Table 7 cross-dataset 'stability' result is unreadable: it reprints Table 6 counts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim to 'demonstrate' that the SAE encodes textual, visual and multimodal concepts in a shared latent space. They also claim their framework improves visual-concept alignment by an average 41% (CLIP) and 45% (ALIGN) while keeping textual concept quality. The conclusion says interventions 'confirm the influence' of the concepts, while the Discussion states they show correlation, not causality.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained SAE concept extraction, external VLM hypothesis generation, and CLIP/ALIGN alignment evaluation on a VLM; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of assigned multimodal concepts changes with the similarity threshold: 223 at 0.70, 132 at 0.80, and 23 at 0.90 (r36-r38).

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping a chosen SAE latent to α=60 qualitatively changes story text. The paper describes the effect as stronger with an image present and strongest for the multimodal concept (one example per modality).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering individual SAE latents in a VLM shifts generated text toward the latent's labelled concept.

fits_no_version.finding: The pipeline labels a subset of SAE latents as multimodal: 132 of 5000 at τ=0.8, a count that is strongly threshold dependent (223 at 0.7, 23 at 0.9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some SAE latents in VLMs respond to the same concept in both image and text tokens.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks
record.problems: The study focuses on a single SAE and a single VLM as explainer; its main analysis uses a subset of LLaVA-NeXT and the first 5000 SAE neurons. The textual evaluation relies on external evaluators, and the paper reports qualitative intervention results without establishing causality. Appendix Table 7 is ambiguous in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible reported results were omitted. Table 7 is retained as an ambiguous flattened result (r45), without assigning its numbers to dataset columns or inferring missing decimal points.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All of it: no capacity competition.
All of it: base-model neurons are not analysed.

Whether the VLM's features are distributed across neurons, or whether the SAE recovers sparse features. Reconstruction, sparsity and monosemanticity of the SAE itself are not evaluated; only explanation-pipeline quality is.
Stability and canonicity of SAE features. The cross-dataset comparison in Table 7 is unreadable (it reprints counts), and completeness is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper: the SAE is a tool, and almost all rows compare explanation pipelines. The reader's V4 'supports' label rests on the study's own method beating a baseline, which does not bear on whether sparse features exist in the model, so it is dropped. The ALIGN category scores (≈16.7 for all categories) look nearly uninformative. Table 7 is a copy-paste error of Table 6.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric structure.
Capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, and feature sharing caused by limited capacity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Tests SAE concept extraction in one VLM setting, not whether features are distributed across many neurons in LLMs generally, nor whether the extracted concepts are complete or ground-truth features.
The paper attempts a cross-dataset similarity/stability analysis, but its displayed results are ambiguous. It does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

relation.reason: Relies on SAE concept extraction as a tool and evaluates explanation quality, rather than testing superposition or dictionary completeness, stability, or canonicality.

tranche.reason: Uses a pretrained SAE to evaluate its concept-explanation and modality-labelling framework. The reported counts and threshold sensitivity measure pipeline assignments; qualitative forced interventions do not independently test a claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 5 specifies 249 SAE neurons within the analysis of the first 5000. Counts depend on agreement between textual and visual hypotheses under both evaluators; they are not independently validated counts of model features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Proposed SAE concept-extraction framework on LLaVA-NeXT-8B-HF, using the LLaVA-NeXT subset and first 5000 SAE neurons
reader_labels.reason: The proposed framework has higher hypothesis–data alignment than the baseline at every reported threshold for both evaluators; see r1-r12. This is evidence of SAE concept extraction in this tested VLM setting, not a general claim about LLMs.
